text:
maria: anyone seen sockets pile up when cancelling async streams?

maria: repro: open stream with short-lived token, break after first chunk. If token refresh triggers mid-stream socket doesn't close.

sam: which python/aiohttp and using built-in refresh?

maria: py3.11.7, aiohttp 3.9.4, built-in refresh. netstat shows many TIME_WAIT after ~50 iterations.

kevin: likely finalizer isn't awaiting ClientResponse.release(). Do you get 'coroutine was never awaited'?

maria: yes sometimes see that. also "RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine" occasionally.

natalie: current stream API returns AsyncIterator but relies on weakref finalizer. we should return an AsyncContextManager that yields an AsyncIterator so cleanup can be awaited. update typing to reflect resource ownership.

sam: workaround: try/finally and await internal close helper (eg await c._transport_close()).

kevin: plan: implement async with pattern: async with client.stream(...) as gen: async for chunk in gen: ... __aexit__ awaits response.close(). Also ensure auth refresh is cancelable and tied to request.

maria: filing bug now and will add repro + logs to issue.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2299 - "async stream: token-refresh mid-stream can leak socket" :white_check_mark:

natalie: i'll own typing/tests. add mypy and aiohttp matrix.

kevin: i'll make a non-breaking shim that warns on GC and nudges users to use async with. include integration test simulating 401 during stream.

sam: please add a small example in examples/ showing graceful cancellation. many users assume break closes connection.

maria: will paste reproducer script in issue. until fix, call response.release()/use async with. :thumbsup:
